To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ray-tracing technique is an appropriate selection technique for virtual environments, since it allows users to select objects in a simple and natural way.
the selection method based on the ray tracing technique is the most suitable one for pSIVE applications, since it is the most efficient in terms of speed, accuracy, and ease of use.

the platform pSIVE allows the construction of virtual environments with associated multimedia information; the platform pSive allows the creation of applications that allow interaction with the virtual world; the selection of elements in the virtual world is done using a ray-tracing technique; the selection technique can be adapted to the hardware used; the selection technique is more efficient with a mouse and keyboard than with a joystick.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of a platform for setting up interactive virtual environments and a comparative study of two variants of a selection technique for the platform.
developing an efficient selection technique that can be used in a variety of applications, and with evaluating the performance of this technique in a virtual environment.
the development of an interactive virtual environment platform, which can be used to build virtual environments for the purpose of virtual tours.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ray-tracing technique is the most suitable for the envisioned applications of the pSIVE platform, since it allows a more natural selection of elements in a virtual environment.
both variants of the ray-casting selection technique have advantages and disadvantages.
the selection technique that best fits pSIVE’s needs is the one that allows users to interact directly with the objects, and that the ray-tracing technique with a single click is the best solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ray-tracing technique is a good choice for virtual environments where users may interact to extract contextual information, since it allows the use of natural movements and it is easy to be adapted to different devices and interaction methods.
we have a platform to create and test interactive virtual environments, and that we have tested two variants of the selection technique for the pSIVE platform.

, in the case of a virtual environment with a large number of 3D objects, ray-casting selection technique is the best choice, while for environments where the number of objects is smaller, ray-sphere selection is more efficient, since the user does not have to aim the cursor at the object to be selected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when using a ray-tracing technique, the user should not be forced to use a specific hand gesture.
the variant that considers the intersection of the ray with the surface normal is more accurate, but the one that uses the intersection of the rays with the object surface is faster.
the ray-tracing technique is a viable solution to select virtual objects in a virtual environment, even if the objects are not visible.
